briefing.briefing: Starting with the GBP picture — sterling (GBPUSD) is essentially flat today, up just +0.01%, and sits at the very top of its 20-day range (100th percentile). Because UK100 and GBP move in opposite directions (a stronger pound makes the index's overseas earnings worth less in sterling terms), this is a quiet but persistent headwind for the index — not a crisis, but a ceiling on upside. The regime right now is a tug-of-war: miners are the bright spot, with copper up +0.87% providing support for the big mining stocks like Rio and Glencore, but energy is dragging in the other direction with Brent crude down -0.76%, which weighs on Shell and BP (two of the index's largest members). Banks are neutral with 10-year gilt yields unchanged on the day, and the pharma sector (dominated by AstraZeneca) is flagged as unpredictable — any stock-specific AZN news could override everything else. On the US side, futures are softer (S&P 500 -0.29%, Nasdaq -1.15%) and gold has surged to a three-month high (+1.38%), which is a classic 'risk-off' signal — meaning investors are nervous and moving toward safer assets. The main headline driving this mood is Iran geopolitical risk combined with pre-US-inflation-data anxiety (Reuters, ~36 minutes ago). The directional bias is moderately bearish (-4 out of 10 on the model's own scale): the ORB (the price range formed in the first 15 minutes after the 08:00 London open) actually broke to the upside this morning, but that move is against the broader bearish backdrop — breaks that go against the day's dominant tone fail more often than they succeed. With 60% of the typical daily range (the average daily move is 85.7 points) already used but only about 79% of daily volume typically done by this time of day, there is still room for afternoon movement — so this is not a 'done' day. Confidence is 5/10: the offsetting forces (copper bullish vs Brent bearish, upside ORB break vs bearish macro) make this genuinely unclear. A clean break and hold above the overnight high of 10,832.2 on rising volume would challenge the bearish view; a slip back below the ORB low of 10,799.5 would confirm it. For the 08:00 ORB trade specifically, today is best read as a fakeout-and-reverse setup — the upside break looks suspect given the macro backdrop, making short entries on a reclaim back below the ORB high (10,819.9) more interesting than chasing long. There are no major UK data events scheduled today, but traders should note a HIGH-impact US PCE inflation print (the Fed's preferred inflation measure) is due Wednesday 26 August at 13:30 BST — this is the week's most important macro risk and could sharply reprice rate expectations. Key levels: overnight high 10,832.2 (first upside resistance), ORB high 10,819.9, ORB low 10,799.5, overnight low 10,799.5 (same level — critical floor), and the prior day low of 10,726 as a stretch target if sellers take control. The single most important thing to remember today: the ORB broke upward, but every major macro signal is pointing the other way — trust the tape only if price holds above 10,832 convincingly.
